definition: Human–robot interaction (HRI) is the study of interactions between humans and robots.
details: Human–robot interaction is a multidisciplinary field with contributions from human–computer interaction, artificial intelligence, robotics, natural language processing, design, psychology and philosophy. A subfield known as physical human–robot interaction (pHRI) has tended to focus on device design to enable people to safely interact with robotic systems.

explainer.lead: Human–robot interaction is the study of interactions between humans and robots. It matters because it is multidisciplinary, drawing on human-computer interaction, AI, robotics, natural language processing, design, psychology, and philosophy.

tiers.eli5: It's the study of how people and robots deal with each other, from how you talk to a robot to how it should behave around you.
tiers.practitioner: Researchers work across HCI, AI, robotics, NLP, design, psychology, and philosophy; a subfield, physical human–robot interaction (pHRI), focuses on device design for safe physical interaction. A pitfall is that safe physical interaction depends on device design, not just software.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as the study of interactions between humans and robots; it is multidisciplinary, and the pHRI subfield focuses on device design to enable people to safely interact with robotic systems.

explainer.example: Designers study how a person safely approaches and physically interacts with a robot, shaping the robot's device design around that interaction.
